finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Unbounded product listing (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: products route calls prisma.product.findMany(...) with include: { colors } and orderBy: { createdAt } but no take/limit/cursor/pagination, and createdAt has no index in schema.  
Impact: At increased QPS this will force full table scans and large sorts, consuming DB CPU/IOPS and network bandwidth and causing severe query latency/timeouts.  
Fix: Add cursor/limit pagination and restrict fields returned; create an index on createdAt (or an appropriate composite index) to avoid costly sorts.

[DB-2] Checkout create-order: missing transaction, coupon race, N+1 writes
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: Coupon is read then updated in separate queries (findUnique then update) and order creation/update + orderItem upserts/deletes are performed outside a single transactional scope, with per-item awaits inside loops for updates/deletes.  
Impact: Concurrent checkouts can overspend limited coupons and produce partial/ inconsistent order state; per-item sequential DB calls amplify query count and latency under load.  
Fix: Enclose coupon check/decrement and order create/update (including item upserts/deletes) in a single transactional block and replace per-item sequential awaits with batched/conditional updates (createMany/updateMany or conditional SQL).

[DB-3] Prisma client not cached in production → connection explosion
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: Code creates new PrismaClient but only assigns it to a global cache when NODE_ENV !== "production", so production runs do not reuse a singleton client.  
Impact: On serverless Next.js deployments this yields many Prisma pools across cold starts/instances and will exhaust Postgres connections, causing connection errors and outages at modest concurrency.  
Fix: Cache PrismaClient on globalThis unconditionally (or use an external pooler like PgBouncer and set small pool sizes) to avoid per-instance pool multiplication.

[DB-4] Stock decrement transaction will create hot-row locks
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: verify-payment runs a prisma.$transaction and inside a loop it updates productColor or product rows to decrement stock per orderItem (multiple row updates inside a long-lived transaction).  
Impact: High concurrent confirms for the same SKU will generate row-level lock contention and blocking, reducing checkout throughput and causing timeouts under load.  
Fix: Use atomic conditional updates (UPDATE ... SET stock = stock - N WHERE id = ... AND stock >= N RETURNING ...) or short SELECT FOR UPDATE+single update, or serialize high-contention SKUs via a queue to avoid long transactions.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-5] Per-request DB ping in cart GET increases load
File: src/app/api/cart/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Cart GET executes await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1` on every request as a health/ping check.  
Impact: This adds an extra round-trip per cart request, increasing DB queries, connection usage and latency at scale (worsening pool exhaustion).  
Fix: Remove per-request ping or memoize/perform infrequent health checks; rely on pooled connection health or monitoring instead.

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] Postgres + Prisma ORM detected
File: prisma/schema.prisma
Evidence: Schema datasource provider = "postgresql" and project uses @prisma/client.
